column2: Taking the great lute with its tuned strings, Hanuman, best of monkeys, went singing to Shiva's presence.
Then, having pleased the Lord of the world with great singing, he worshipped the God's feet with pure brihati flowers.
Then Shankara, Soul of the universe, pleased, in the presence of the sages, of the demons, gods and kings,
gave him the boon of life until the end of the kalpa, the power to leap across, mastery of the scriptures, and increase of strength.
Thus, O best of Brahmins, Hanuman, having received a boon from the great-souled Maheshvara directly in my sight, was overjoyed.
Adorned with all ornaments, with his own splendour outshining the splendour of the gods, of gracious form, youthful, a portion of Shiva, he honoured all the gods.
Hanuman was ordered there, the lord of sages, to serve me; and I too know him by Maheshvara, the moon-crested.
What more need be said, O Brahmin sage? As the Lord of monkeys is in intellect, in justice and in firmness, there is no other like him anywhere.
Thus the whole account, destroying sin for those who read or hear it, has been told to you; go, O Brahmin, at ease.
Hearing the words of the wise Ramabhadra, Lord of the Raghus, circumambulating him and bowing, I came back as I had come.
Thus this account of Hanuman has been told to you, O Brahmin — giving happiness and liberation, the essence; what else do you wish to hear?

Beautiful, with the grace of cheeks shining with swaying earrings, with a gentle smile and fair nose, clad in fine gold-coloured garments, divine ornaments, anointed with unguents, with tinkling nets of bells —

holding a flute in his hand and blowing it, with a conch in the left, a staff, of noble dress, and the right hand skilled in granting desires: one should worship the son of Nanda, meditating thus, for the attainment of Lakshmi.
Having so meditated, the best Vaishnava should worship Krishna as before; he should prepare an offering of cakes, milk-rice and other food.
Having offered a hundred and eight oblations with milk-rice and ghee, he should give the offering in the respective directions and then give water for sipping.
The best Vaishnava who worships Krishna at midday should chant the best mantra a thousand and eight times.
All gods bow to him; he is dear to the world; endowed with intelligence, long life, prosperity and beauty, he grows with sons and grandsons.
In the third time of worship there is a difference in time: some of the wise say in the evening or at night.
Others say: with the ten-syllable at night, with the eighteen-syllable in the evening, or he should do both with both.
In the evening at Dvaravati, adorned with variegated gardens, set with eight thousand mansions,
in a best mansion surrounded by lakes with dark water, with lotuses, blue lilies, swans and cranes,
in a circle of glorious jewels with rising bright lustre, seated on a golden lotus seat is Krishna, bewildering the three worlds,
surrounded by hosts of sages for the decision of the truth of the Self, pointing out to those sages his own supreme imperishable abode,
dark as a blossoming blue lotus, his eyes long as lotus petals, tender, with curls mixed with his crown and forest-garland,
with a charming gracious face, shining shark-shaped earrings, the Shrivatsa on his chest, shining Kaustubha, most lovely,
with a breast tawny as saffron, in yellow silk garments, adorned with necklace, armlets, bracelets and girdle,
who has taken away the great burden of the Earth, joyful in mind, with four arms shining with conch, discus, mace and lotus.
Having so meditated, the mantra-knower should worship; the first enclosure is the limbs; the second with the queens; in the third he should worship:
Narada, Parvata, Jishnu, Nishatha, Uddhava, Daruka, Vishvaksena, Shaineya, and in front in the directions the son of Vinata (Garuda),
and the best Vaishnava should worship the guardians of the world and Vajra and the rest. Having thus worshipped by rule, he should offer milk-rice.
Having satisfied (the Lord) here with water thought of as milk mixed with sugar, the mantra-knower should chant a hundred and eight times, meditating on the Supreme Person.
In all worship, the offering should be made at noon or otherwise; from the seat to the arghya, having praised him, the wise one should bow.
Having dismissed the Self, capable, and placed it in his own heart-lotus, becoming one with him, he should again worship the Self.
He who worships Vasudeva thus every evening obtains all desires and at the end attains the highest goal.
At night, if the mind is overcome by love, he should worship Nanda's son, wearied by the Rasa dance, in the middle of the circle of gopis,
cooled by gentle winds laden with dust from blooming kunda, kahlara and jasmine flowers,
(a long verse describing the moonlit night on the bank of the Kalindi, bees humming, with the flute sounding, Mukunda smiling),
(describing Krishna: dark as rain-clouds, with eyes long as lotus, lips like bimba fruit, peacock-feather crest, shining earrings),

(continuing: adorned with girdle, anklets, necklace, bracelets, armlets, wearing a garland of forest flowers between two gopis, eager for the Rasa play, struck by love) — one should meditate on Mukunda.
(The musical notes of the Rasa dance — seven notes in many ways — and Krishna's lovely body ringing with the ornaments.)
(In the Rasa play arranged by groups of women with joined hands, Krishna took many forms to be with each of them.)
Having so meditated, the mantra-knower should worship; the first enclosure is the limbs. One desiring prosperity, the best Vaishnava, with the digits and lotuses with the vowels,
should worship sixteen couples such as Keshava-Kirti; then Indra and the rest and Vajra and the rest.
(The Rasa gathering: a broad, round, smooth post a span high is planted in the ground; stepping on it with feet and clasping hands with others, this is the Rasa gathering.)
Having so worshipped, with milk, sugar, flesh... and ghee, offering with the offering of food and with cups in royal number,
the mantra-knower should offer to each pair in order; having done the rest as before, he should chant a thousand.
Having praised, bowed and prayed, he should complete the remainder of the worship. He who thus worships Krishna would attain the state of prosperity.
He becomes lord of the eight powers beginning with anima, without doubt; having enjoyed various pleasures here, at the end he goes to Vishnu's abode.
Thus when the mantra is perfected by worship and the rest, he should accomplish desired aims; or the wise one should worship three times, twenty-eight times,
and satisfy again the attendants, as laid down for each time: in the morning with curd mixed with jaggery; at noon with milk;
and in the evening with butter; the best Vaishnava should again satisfy with milk mixed with sugar candy.
I satisfy should be added at the end of the mantra to each of the names; at the end of the second he should complete the rest of the worship.
Having sprinkled himself with the water of that offering, he should drink the water; then having dismissed that satisfied one, absorbed in him, he should chant the mantra.
Now the materials for desire-rites and for tarpana are told; relying on the rules told, he should use any one of them.
Milk-rice, curd-preparation, ghee, jaggery-rice, kricara, milk, curds, banana, plantain, tamarind, menstruous (?),
cakes, sweets, parched grain, flattened rice, butter — these sixteen substances were told by Brahma and the others.
Having offered flattened rice at the end of parched grain, and sugar candy, he who thus satisfies seventy-four times each morning,
meditating on Krishna's feet, the mantra-knower obtains the desired within the circle. With milk heated from the stream, butter and curds,
milk-mango, ghee, sugar candy, honey and curd-cake: he should worship with nine substances, each twelve times.
Thus the best Vaishnava who again performs the satisfying a hundred and eight times obtains the fruit stated before.
What need of more? This tarpana gives all desires: with water thought of as milk mixed with sugar and hot from the stream,
the practitioner satisfying Krishna, going to a village, obtains wealth, clothes and food with his retinue.
As many times as the mantra-knower satisfies, so many times he should chant the mantra. By tarpana alone he accomplishes all his tasks.
Now I shall tell the desire-offerings for the good of practitioners. The mantra-knower desiring prosperity should offer with flowers of Shri, (to gain) an unblamable wealth;
with ghee and food for increase of ghee-rice; with wild flowers Brahmins; with jasmine flowers kings;
with black flowers Vaishyas; with blue lilies Shudras; with salt all; with lotuses a young woman he should subdue.
The offering in cow-sheds with milk-rice and ghee quickly makes peace for cows; the cowherd becomes lord of the cow-herd.
Meditating on Krishna in the dress of a student, adorned with nets of bells, the mantra-knower should satisfy him with water thought of as milk.
Pleased, he gives wealth, grain, sons and fame. With Brahma-tree fuel-sticks, kusha, or sesame and rice,
the mantra-knower should offer ten thousand soaked in the three sweet things in the fire; he should subdue Brahmins; with royal-tree flowers
Kshatriyas, with kuranda flowers Vaishyas; and with patala flowers the wise one should subdue the last (Shudras).
With white lotuses, red lotuses, champaka and patala flowers in order, having offered ten thousand with three sweet things, he subdues the best women.
With hayari flowers soaked in three sweet things at midnight daily, the wise one properly offering for eight days would subdue the best women.
At night, thirty thousand with mustard seeds soaked in the three sweet things; offering daily for a month, even the lord of gods becomes subject.
Having brought the clothes of milkmaids, and climbing a kadamba tree, he should remember Krishna and chant a thousand at night.
The practitioner would quickly draw even Urvashi by force. What more need be said? This mantra subdues all.
Now I shall tell the supreme secret, giving liberation to men: he should meditate in his heart-lotus on the Lord, son of Devaki.

I bow to Murari, glorious, white as jasmine and the moon, lotus-eyed, bearing conch and discus, mace and lotus in his lotus hands, shining with a garland of fresh lotuses, to be known by the best of sages, charming with divine ornaments, radiant with divine anointing, destroyer of all fear, clad in yellow.

Having thus meditated on that Primal Person seated on the open heart-lotus seat, golden and wonderful with the colour of a dense cloud, one should chant twelve hundred thousand. One of the two mantras, with Om twice between, he should offer a thousand with fuel of milk-trees as stated, with honey, ghee and sugar, or with milk-rice.
Thus meditating daily in his heart-lotus on Krishna worshipped by the lords of the world, the mantra-knower should chant the mantra three thousand times.
Having worshipped by the rule stated for the evening, and again made the offering, by the rule stated before, his mind fixed on him,
the wise one who thus constantly worships the son of Nanda the cowherd crosses the ocean of samsara and goes to the highest state.

(A yantra described in coded terms: in the middle, in the outer parts, within a fire-city figure, in the pericarp he should write Kandarpa with the object; the six-syllable of the enemy in the filaments; the power Shri and the first; the ten-syllable best mantra, one letter to each petal.)
Enclosed by an earth-house, with a garland of Manmatha, written with gorochana by a golden needle on a silk cloth, made into a pellet: this Gopala-yantra is declared to give all desires.

Worn after being sprinkled with water and consecrated by the great, it alone is able to subdue the three worlds; it is of unmeasured power for protection, fame, sons, land, wealth, grain, Lakshmi and good fortune.
Smara (kleem), "Trivikrama", "Akrishtyai" for the heart: this six-syllable is declared the mantra giving all success.
Kroda with peace, moon and fire — the seed Maya; "Govinda" with fire and moon; the mantra declared the Shri seed.
By these two, an eighteen-syllable mantra and a twenty-syllable mantra arise. In the Shaligrama, a jewel, a yantra, a circle, or in images,
the worship of Hari should be daily done and not only on the ground. Those who thus worship Krishna attain the highest goal.
The sage of the twenty-syllable is Brahma, metre Gayatri; the deity is Krishna; the seed is Kama; the power is "dvitha".
The limbs are conceived with the syllables Rama-Agni-Veda-Veda-sea-eyes. Having made it all-pervading with the root, then with the mantra enclosed,
attentive, he should place the letters of the alphabet in their respective places; having placed the ten principles, he should make it all-pervading with the root.
Then he should do the mantra-placing for success in the deity's state: on head, forehead, between the brows, eyes, ears,
nose, face, chin, throat, root of the arms, heart, belly, navel, organ, root-lotus,
waist, knees, shanks, ankles, feet, in order — placing the mantras ending in the heart: this is declared the placing of creation.
On the heart, belly, navel, organ, root-lotus, waist, knees, shanks, ankles and feet likewise,
on head, cheeks, between brows, eyes, ears, nose, face, chin, throat and root of arms he should place in order
the mantra letters ending in "namah": this is declared the placing of preservation. On feet, ankles, shanks, knees,
waist, root, banner, navel, belly, heart again, root of arms, throat, chin, face, nose,
ears, eyes, between brows, forehead, head — he should place the mantra letters: this is called the placing of dissolution.
Having done the placing of creation and preservation again, the best Vaishnava should then place the "cage of forms" as before.
Again having done the six limbs, he should meditate on Krishna in the heart-lotus, in Dvaravati, with best mansions shining like a thousand suns,
surrounded by many wish-trees, in a jewelled pavilion with blazing jewel pillars, doors, arches and walls,
with canopies of pearls hanging in full-blown variegated flowers, in the middle with floors of ruby and heaps of gems,
below trees rich in streams of continuously falling gems, the quarters lit by rows of jewel lamps,
seated on a lotus-throne of jewel lions, bright as rising sun, Achyuta is to be meditated on, like molten gold,
with the radiance of ten million moons and suns risen together with lightning; handsome in all limbs, gentle, adorned with all ornaments,
clothed in yellow, with a lotus-like hand shining with conch, discus, mace, touching a pot of unceasing streams of shining gems,
with the toe of his left lotus foot rivalling the colour of a bud; on his head, Rukmini and Satyabhama, at his right and left,
sprinkling with streams of gems from pots in their hands; Nagnajiti and Sunanda giving them pots;
Mitravinda and Sulakshmana on the right and left, lifting gem-filled jars from the river of gems;
Jambavati and Sushila giving them on the right and left; outside, sixteen thousand beloveds all around,
to be meditated on, bright with pots shining with streams of gold and gems; outside them the eight treasures filling the earth with wealth;
outside them all the Vrishnis, with the vowels as before. Having so meditated, he should chant five hundred thousand and a tenth part,
offering with red lotuses, and worship on the seat stated before. Anointing with perfumed paste, he should draw an eight-petalled lotus,
in the pericarp a hexagon with Manmatha and the object; with the remaining seventeen syllables he should enclose the vowel.
In the corners east, south-west and north-west Shri; in the remaining ones Samvid; in the six junctions and six corners, thrice each on the filaments,
he should write the Smara Gayatri; the Mala mantra on the eight petals; having written six "ushas", outside it enclosed by the letters of the alphabet.
Outside he should draw the earth-disc, with Shri and Maya in the directions and corners; the earth-square adorned with eight thunderbolts.
This yantra, written as before on golden and other plates and consecrated, whoever wears is worshipped even by the gods.
The Gayatri: "Kamadevaya vidmahe pushpabanaya dhimahi; Tan no 'nangah prachodayat."
To be chanted at the start of the chanting of the Gopala mantras, pleasing to people: "Kamadevaya" ending with the heart, "Sarvajanapriya".
At the end of "sarvajana" the word "sammohana"; "jvala jvala prajvala" and of all people,
hridayam mama he should say, "vasham kuru kuru" for the head: the Madana mantra is declared of forty-eight syllables.
At the start of the chant, the Kama seed at its beginning subdues the three worlds. Having worshipped the seat as before and conceived the form with the root,
invoking Achyuta there with devotion, he should worship him in complete form, from the seat to the ornaments, and by the sequence of placing again,
creation, preservation, the six limbs, crown, a pair of earrings, conch, discus, mace, lotus, garland, Shrivatsa and Kaustubha,
the best Vaishnava, having worshipped with perfume and flowers by the root, should worship the six limbs in the six corners and in the petals of the directions in order.
Vasudeva and the others in the corners, then Shanti and the rest; the best practitioner should worship the eight queens at the petal-tips.
Then he should worship the sixteen thousand beloveds at once: Indranila, Mukunda, Karala, Ananda, Kachchhapa,
conch, lotus, then the Padma treasure — the eight treasures in order; outside them the guardians of the world and Vajra and the rest.
Having thus respectfully worshipped Krishna surrounded by seven enclosures, he should satisfy him with milk mixed with curd, sugar-candy and ghee.
Having given divine services, praised and bowed to Keshava, he should dismiss him into his own heart with his retinue.
Having placed the Self and worshipped, the wise one, absorbed in him, should move about. The gem-anointing, meditation and worship of the twenty-syllable are told.
He who thus worships this mantra becomes a seat of prosperity. He who chants this mantra with chanting, offering, worship and meditation,
his house is filled with gems and gold and grain continually; the earth in his hand is full of all crops.
Rich with sons and friends he goes at the end to the highest goal. Having worshipped Govinda in the fire with white flowers and rice,
having offered ten thousand soaked in ghee, he should put the ash on his head; he gets abundance of food and the like, and all women come under his control.
With red lotuses soaked in three sweet things, offering a hundred thousand attentively, Indra's lordship becomes to him like a blade of grass, surely.
He who daily offers a thousand and eight white flowers soaked in three sweet things becomes within a month the royal priest of a king.
By this mantra he should accomplish these and other applications. Now I shall tell the king of mantras of ten syllables, giving all success:
Smriti with "sadya", "sakshi", "lohita", "janavallabha", "pavana", ending with "agnipriya": the ten-syllable mantra is declared.
Narada is its sage; its metre Virat; Krishna is its deity; Kama the seed; Vahnijaya (svaha) the power, say the wise.
Achakra, vichakra, suchakra, then "Trailokyarakshana-chakra", "Asurantaka-chakra":
with these wheels, with the dative endings and two "tha", the five limbs of the mantra are conceived. Then, having made the mantra pervade, enclosed in Om, on the two hands thrice,
he should place the mantra syllables ending in the heart, with the moon, interleaved by Om, from the right thumb to the left thumb on the finger joints.
This is the placing of creation; now the placing of preservation: he should place from the left little finger to the little finger in preservation.
From the left thumb to the right thumb in dissolution; dissolution is declared to destroy the mass of faults.
Creation-ending gives learning to students of pure mind; preservation-ending is for householders, thus in the form of desire-rites and the like;
dissolution-ending is for lords of sages and for the wholly dispassionate. Again in the order of preservation he should place the syllables on the fingers.
